recommendation: Keep the empty no-change audit commit. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-14009 unless the work group makes a new substantive decision about canonical URL naming.
issue_request: FHIR-14009 asked to rename ValueSet.url to ValueSet.uri and adjust the ValueSet/$expand url parameter because implementers confused canonical identifiers with literal retrieval URLs. The final Published / Not Persuasive with Modification resolution kept the url name to encourage actual/resolvable URLs and called for documentation improvements.
initial_application: The Jira comment records an SVN application, and git history contains 9a720ed103130ae2b7de480d307c57f08b80d4e8, '#14009 - better doco about url vs uri'. That commit updated ValueSet and CodeSystem identification narrative plus shared metadata-resource URL wording instead of renaming the element or parameter.
additional_context: ValueSet is active in source/fhir.ini and its operation list references OperationDefinition/ValueSet-expand. Later commit 6f7c3716ef8e176e5ea811ceb12844b81a3904ec standardized surrounding terminology from canonical URI to canonical URL, and FHIR-50825/36cac9d84ce5e9d184a2532490bf06411048793a later clarified the same $expand url parameter to reference the canonical URL while keeping type uri. FHIR-22699 fixed a ValueSet.url typo and is already represented on the combined branch. Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source already says ValueSet.url is the canonical URL, explains that it is named url rather than uri for legacy reasons and to encourage a resolvable URL when possible, keeps the underlying canonical-resource type as uri, and describes ValueSet/$expand url as a reference to the canonical URL of a value set.

related_jiras.note: Later Applied vocab decision on the same ValueSet/$expand url parameter; it confirms the current wording should reference the canonical URL while keeping type uri.
Later Published ValueSet.url typo correction; already represented on the combined branch, so no duplicate commit was made here.
